sections.text:
Quad Cities Superintendent Notice No. 12 
Page | 1  
 
                                                  
 
 
January 1, 2025 
 
SUBDIVISIONS: 
Chicago, Davenport, Eldridge, Kansas City, Marquette, Nitrin, Ottumwa, 
Rockford, Laredo 
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 
1-12 
NOTICES CANCELLED:    
 
SUBJECT: 
Location Information 
 
 
Clinton 
Crews working at Clinton ADM facility:   
• 
MUST WEAR HARDHATS when outside the cab of the locomotive while on ADM property.  
 
BEFORE ENTERING ADM: 
• 
Crews MUST HAVE a portable radio with ADM’s frequency. 
 
• 
Crews MUST CONTACT the ADM switch crew via radio.  
 
Anyone that does not have the required hardhat or the required radio frequency MUST contact the Trainmaster on duty or Road Foreman, 
to become compliant. 
Your cooperation in this matter is appreciated and expected.  
All South bound trains: 
Southbound Trains at Clinton: Procedure to cross or interchange with the UP at the UP manual interlocking at 5th Street, Clinton, IA. 
 
Goal:  Mitigate blocking public crossings 
 
Southbound trains:  After obtaining TW from the CP Dispatcher at Deer Creek, inform the UP Dispatcher what time you can arrive at 
5th Street, but remain at Deer Creek until commitment received from the UP Dispatcher of what time the UP will have a signal to proceed 
at 5th Street. 
 
When given time of signal, pace train to arrive at 5th Street at that designated time.  If signal not given by UP Dispatcher as instructed, 
contact UP Dispatcher and notify CP Dispatcher immediately. 
 
Empty coal trains are to be governed by the following:  If Cab signals fail to test properly, advance train to Camanche Siding.

sections.title: SN 12: Location Information
sections.text:
Quad Cities Superintendent Notice No. 12 
Page | 2  
 
 
Mason City Subdivision 
 
Priority Crossing Notification Protocol 
 
Management met jointly with the Union Pacific local leadership and the local municipalities, relative to the development of various 
protocols around blocked crossings. These protocols specifically identified arterial routes through the community that are mainly utilized 
by emergency response crews and considered critical routes.  
 
The routes by carrier are as follows: 
 
Union Pacific – 1st Street NW and Federal Avenue (Rockwell Subdivision). 
 
Canadian Pacific/DM&E – Highway #122, Kentucky Avenue, Taft Avenue & Federal Avenue (Rockwell Subdivision). 
 
When trains are stopped in excess of 10 minutes, or trains are stopped and it is anticipated that the duration may exceed 10 minutes, 
the train crew is required to contact the Mason City ATM.  State who you are, the railroad you represent, the crossing affected and the 
duration and/or event that is creating the blocked crossing.  
 
The Mason City ATM will in turn contact the MCPD dispatcher at (641) 421 3001.  The dispatcher will notify the appropriate parties to 
ensure that alternate routes are utilized if necessary. 
 
Crew members are to notify the Mason City ATM when the obstruction is cleared.  
 
 
Fruitland 
 
Coal Train Reporting 
 
Effective immediately, any crew that services the Fruitland coal plant will provide the Network Service Center a copy of their Train Delay 
Report faxed to 888-766-7245.  The following information will be required in addition to information already provided: 
• 
Plant arrival / spot time 
• 
Crew expired HOS time 
• 
Crew time on train if relieving at plant 
• 
Release / pull time from plant 
• 
Specific times sitting idle for plant breakdowns 
• 
Specific times sitting idle for any CP caused delays 
 
 
Ottumwa 
 
Empty Coal Trains 
 
 
Effective immediately - All empty coal trains destined to the BNSF at Ottumwa must have the middle locomotives moved to the head 
end of the train prior to leaving the unloading facility. When the train arrives Ottumwa, the inbound crew will have the locomotives 
configured so the rear most DP unit is facing North for delivery to the BNSF.

sections.title: SN 12: Location Information
sections.text:
Quad Cities Superintendent Notice No. 12 
Page | 3  
 
 
Muscatine 
GPC 
Effective Immediately - Any crew going to the back side of GPC in Muscatine, IA, will need to contact the GPC Security Guard on 
channel AAR 094-094, 30 minutes prior to arrival to insure the GPC train crews are clear of the area and the gate can be opened.   
Once leaving GPC backside contact the GPC Security Guard again on AAR 094-094 to advise of departure.   
All Crews: 
Effective immediately:  All crew working Muscatine must contact the Nahant ATM via the radio to confirm work, car locations, and 
completion of work, prior to arriving or leaving Muscatine. 
The tone up is **7366#.   
The RTI radio disconnect is *#.  
As a reminder – you are on the radio not just a telephone. 
Muscatine Reporting: 
All crews working Muscatine or SSAB are required to turn in their completed Work Order, F-125 Form, and/or Switch Lists prior to going 
off duty to ensure inventory can be accurately tracked. This procedure contributes to the timely and efficient movement of our customer’s 
cars by correctly reporting the exact location of each car.     
These forms must be faxed to Customer Service at 888-766-7245 and the Nahant ATM at 563-322-2852.   
Assignments include: 
KU81, KU82, KU83, KU84, K70, K71, K72, 260, 261 and any other train crew performing work at these locations.  
100% compliance with these instructions is required.  If non-compliance is discovered, disciplinary actions may be applied.     
Lower Yard: 
Effective immediately, when kicking cars in the Lower Yard in Muscatine, IA into track LY07 through LY11: 
When releasing only empty cars, make the cut to release the cars around the 2 track switch since they will slow down through the curves. 
When releasing loaded cars, make the cut to release the cars short of the 7 track switch since they gain speed and could couple faster 
than 4 MPH.

SUBJECT: 
Air Tablet Reporting on All Trains 
 
 
All Assistant Engineers and Conductors: 
 
In an effort to reduce locomotive & car dwell employees are to be using their air tablets on All Trains. Effective immediately the assistant 
engineer or conductor are responsible to properly use and accurately execute their air tablets before tie up. 
 
You have been issued the tools and will be held accountable for all air tablet reporting.  
 
If you are unable to login the Air Help desk will assist in getting a username and password reset. They will also be able to walk you 
through how to use the Air Tablet. 
 
Air Help Desk- 1-888-947-8117 
 
If you cannot get the tablet to work after contacting the Help Desk you must obtain an authorization number for reporting on an F125 
form. Note the authorization number on the F125 and send the completed form to Customer Service. 
 
If you DO NOT currently have/or have access to an iPad, you must contact the manager on duty so they can contact the 
Airtab Desk to get a SD Number for your train. This will be required every time you come on duty until you are supplied with 
an iPad.

sections.title: SN 1: Employee Expectations
sections.text:
Quad Cities Superintendent Notice No. 1 
Page | 1  
 
                                                  
 
 
January 1, 2025 
 
SUBDIVISIONS: 
Chicago, Davenport, Eldridge, Kansas City, Marquette, Nitrin, Ottumwa, 
Rockford, Laredo 
NOTICES IN EFFECT: 
1 
NOTICES CANCELLED:    
 
SUBJECT: 
Quad Cities Employee Expectations 
 
 
• Instructions for all Crews working Local Assignments on the Quad Cities Division 
 
Effective immediately, all Crews working Local Assignments are instructed as follows: 
 
• 
You will contact the ATM or Trainmaster on duty at the end of your shift. 
• 
You will be required to turn in a fully documented Train Delay Form noting any delays over fifteen (15) minutes. 
o In times where you are delayed by the Dispatcher not answering, contact will be attempted every ten (10) minutes until 
contact is made and directions are given. Each one of these contact times must be documented on your Train Delay Form. 
 
If there are no ATM/Trainmaster on duty, there will be designated drop boxes/bins that you are to turn in your Train Delay Forms at the 
depots. 
 
• Removing Trash from Locomotives 
 
Crews are responsible for removing their trash and ensuring the locomotives are clean of trash at crew change locations.  Trash bags 
will be available at Marquette, Dubuque, Savanna, Nahant, Ottumwa, and Kansas City.   
Outbound crews will need to take a trash bag with them for their trip and remove it when their tour of duty is complete. When removing 
trash bags, ensure they are disposed of in a proper location.  We will not leave them on the ground at the crew change location.  This is 
in an effort to provide a clean work environment for the next crew and to help stop the spread of disease.   
 
• Tie Up Instructions 
 
Effective immediately all crews working through the Quad Cities Terminals (Road Crews & Local Assignments) are required to check in 
with the Supervisor on duty and provide your off-duty time. 
 
***If you have an assigned job and work over 12 hours you are expected to show on your rest for your job the following 
day.***

sections.title: SN 1: Employee Expectations
sections.text:
Quad Cities Superintendent Notice No. 1 
Page | 2  
 
• Crews Tying Up Before 10 and After 10/12 Hours 
 
It has come to our attention that employees are entering the depot and not tying up when their work is completed. Effective 
immediately, once your work is completed and there are no further tasks/instructions to be performed and you’ve spoken with the 
Supervisor on duty you will tie up immediately. 
 
***Engineers when you have completed your tasks per the instructions set by this notice, YOU DO NOT need to wait for your 
assistant engineer/conductor to finish their work or tie up before you tie up.*** 
 
Locomotive Engineers, Assistant Engineers and Conductors tying up are not authorized to tie-up in less than 10 hours unless 
instructed to do so from their respective Supervisor. 
 
Locomotive Engineers, Assistant Engineers and Conductors working a 10 hour assignment and are tying up past 10 hours will need to 
explain their reasons for tying up past their 10 hours to the Supervisor on duty. 
 
Locomotive Engineers, Assistant Engineers and Conductors working a 12 hour assignment and are tying up past 12 hours will need to 
explain their reasons for tying up past their 12 hours to the Supervisor on duty. 
 
If you have any questions on any of the instructions please contact your supervisor on duty for clarification.

SUBJECT: 
Blocked Crossings Across the Quad Cities (Updated May 16, 2025) 
 
 
Blocked crossings impact the public and customers across the Quad Cities.  Effective immediately, all crews working around and over 
road crossings must not block the crossing while performing work. 
Crew responsibilities:  
• 
Plan work to remain clear of crossings  
• 
If switching involves working over a road crossing, clear the crossing regularly to permit movement of traffic  
• 
Communicate with train dispatcher if work event requires cutting crossings or cutting farther from regular work location to 
eliminate blocking crossings  
• 
Train crews that have been notified that a meet is planned, you will be required to ask the dispatcher what time the opposing 
train will arrive and pace your train. This will allow you to reduce blocking crossings in communities. 
• 
All crews working in the Luke Yard at Muscatine between the hours of 07:15 and 08:15 will be prohibited from blocking the 
crossing at Fruitland, IA on the Ottumwa Sub MP 225.56. 
• 
Gaines Street (Ball Park Crossing) in Downtown Davenport cannot be blocked for any reason. 
 
It is our responsibility to respect the communities we operate in.  Plan work accordingly.
